ground_truth.description: Changed .unwrap_or(text) to .unwrap(). The original code gracefully handled malformed string nodes (from error recovery) by falling back to the raw text. The .unwrap() will panic on any string that doesn't have matching double quotes — this includes error-recovery nodes, single-quoted strings, and template literals that reach this codepath.

lower_single_quoted_string() uses .unwrap() on the quote-stripping chain. If the tree-sitter node text doesn't have matching single quotes (e.g., unterminated string literal), this will panic. Should use .unwrap_or(text) or return None for graceful degradation.
lower_single_quoted_string() is defined but there's no corresponding case in the lower_expr() match dispatch for single-quoted strings. The function will never be called from the main lowering path.

task.title: Lower single-quoted string literals in the tree-sitter parser
task.description: Reify sources can write string literals with single quotes, but `TsParser` in `crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs` only lowers the double-quoted `string_literal` node kind, so a `'text'` literal never reaches `ExprKind::StringLiteral` and downstream evaluation sees nothing. Add `lower_single_quoted_string` next to `lower_string_literal` and wire single-quoted literals through the same expression-lowering path. Observable outcome: `'abc'` and `"abc"` in a .rfy source produce the same `Expr` — `ExprKind::StringLiteral("abc")` with the span of the literal node — so the two quote styles are interchangeable everywhere a string literal is accepted today.
task.test_strategy: Add `reify-syntax` unit tests that parse a binding for each quote style and assert both yield `ExprKind::StringLiteral` with the same payload and a span covering the literal node, plus a case where a single-quoted literal appears nested inside a larger expression. Re-run the existing `reify-syntax` parser suites to confirm no regression: `cargo test -p reify-syntax`.
